title: What if you grew 1 inch every day?
caption:
What if Dave grew one inch taller every day? One year later: 11 metres tall. Then physics shows up. 📏
The square-cube law: grow 6x in every direction and your weight goes up 216x, but your bones only get 36x stronger.
Would you take the height anyway? Yes or absolutely not?
first_comment: King Kong would collapse under his own weight before he ever climbed a building. Prove me wrong 🦍📏
sources: Galileo Galilei, 'Two New Sciences' (Discorsi, 1638), Day Two: scaling a structure up makes it weaker relative to its weight; giant animals would need disproportionately thick bones
J. B. S. Haldane, 'On Being the Right Size' (1926): weight grows with the cube of size while bone strength grows with the cross-section (the square)
Arithmetic: 1.8 m + 1 inch x 365 days = about 11 m, about 6.2x taller; 6^3 = 216, 6^2 = 36, so stress on the bones rises about 6x
